subject: Owner-directed reorg: Mac = local brain, cloud = cloud brain, coexisting + communicating in REAL TIME both ways — plus the Docker reliability fix and a docker/podman engine split you should know about
body:
The owner asked for a clearer operating model and flagged that the two lanes must communicate in real time, both ways, always. This is that message. Please keep the mailbox channel warm and surface what you're doing back to the Mac the same way — he wants us feeding each other, not running blind in parallel.

THE MODEL (owner's words, made concrete). Mac = the LOCAL BRAIN: it owns everything only it can do — Docker/containers, the iOS builds + simulator, the macOS MCP, the live-vendor connectors. Cloud = the CLOUD BRAIN. They COEXIST and feed each other; neither is retired. They meet at origin, never in a shared working directory. The one hard rule that stops the collisions we've been hitting: ONE session per checkout. The recent branch-switch-under-each-other mess came from two sessions editing the same Mac folder at once — not from anything in git.

WHAT I JUST DID ON THE MAC (all owner-authorized cleanup + a build):
- Removed two STALE duplicate clones from ~/Downloads (a July-19 checkout 445 commits behind, + an extracted iOS app) — 885 MB, moved to Trash, nothing was using them. Only one canonical checkout remains: Public/Projects/SignalGrid/SignalGrid-Review-Hub.
- Pruned dead Docker containers: 23 -> 9, reclaiming 48.9 GB. They were ad-hoc orphans (random names, no lifecycle owner) from many run-live-lanes/manual runs.
- Built sg-stack (branch mac/sg-stack-docker-reliability, PR incoming, preflight running): one idempotent manager — up | status | down | restart-policy | install-autostart. It wraps run-live-lanes.sh (not a reimplementation) and adds the three missing things: a credential-helper fix, a reboot-survival restart policy, and honest status/teardown. A launchd agent starts Docker Desktop on login so the local brain is ready with no session open.

TWO THINGS YOU NEED TO KNOW, because they affect what CI/cloud can assume:

1. THE CREDENTIAL-HELPER HANG, now fixed. Docker Desktop writes credsStore="desktop"; a headless `docker pull`/`run` calls that helper, which wants a GUI prompt, so from a Claude/launchd/ssh shell it HANGS forever instead of failing. That is the "won't run the image/container" symptom. scripts/lib/docker-credhang-guard.sh points DOCKER_CONFIG at a helper-less config ONLY when credsStore="desktop" and the caller hasn't set DOCKER_CONFIG — no-op on Linux/CI/podman. Wired into run-live-lanes.sh before its first docker call. If your macOS CI runners ever hang on a live-lane pull, this is why and this is the fix.

2. A DOCKER vs PODMAN ENGINE SPLIT that is a live inconsistency. On this Mac BOTH are running: Docker Desktop AND a podman 6.0.2 machine. scripts/lib/container-engine.sh prefers podman ("the chosen runtime"), but every actual sg-* container lives in DOCKER, and podman holds none. So a blind sg_resolve_engine manages the empty podman and reports the docker containers as missing — which is a bug I worked around in sg-stack (it targets the engine that actually holds the containers, and forces run-live-lanes onto the same one so they can't split-brain). But the underlying doctrine-vs-reality split is real and is yours to adjudicate: is the lab supposed to be podman (then why are the containers in docker) or docker (then container-engine.sh's preference is wrong)? Pick one; right now new bring-ups can land in a different engine than the existing containers depending on whether the podman machine happens to be up.

STILL PENDING, owner-gated: a handful of dead local branches (bench-decision-throughput, mac/ponytail-native-cuts, mac/stack-reference-skill, worktree-mac-lane-work) that squash-landed and need a force-delete the Mac's hook blocks for an agent — the owner runs it. And fix/ios-enterpriseshell-build-and-run (104 commits, 6 weeks old, superseded by the SwiftUI rebuild) — probably dead, unverified, kept for now.

Nothing here changes lib/, the decision core, the /v1 surface, or any launch claim. It is Mac-lane operability only.
